trickyParts: The pane this implementer ran in has the released extension, whose handoff-complete rule refuses any bash command whose text names the three words of the shell completion: the acceptance-2 pattern file was written with the write tool, a commit message naming `jj undo` was refused by the operation-log rule and rephrased, and the deep-workers were told to search for the phrase with the grep tool.

The pin's `edit` tool takes one string input in the hashline form (`[path#TAG]\nPUT 1.=1:\n+text`), and every tool requires an `i` intent field (additionalProperties false); the real-OMP test builds the edit from the previous turn's read result header.
The harness pins the pane's PATH to <bin>:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, so the test symlinks the jj it finds (Bun.which) into the pane's bin: in CI jj lives in ~/.local/bin.
